nodes.name: Sunlight
nodes.desc: Energy for the forest; open pine stands on the upper slopes get far more light than the shaded cloud forest below.

nodes.name: Cloud and rain
nodes.desc: Moist air rising over the high peaks feeds the humid broadleaf cloud forest and the streams that drain the massif.

nodes.name: Fire
nodes.desc: Frequent fires, often set by people, favour pine seedlings and kill young broadleaf trees, shifting the forest boundary.

nodes.name: Limestone soil
nodes.desc: Karst limestone terrain holds thin soils and nutrients that forest plants draw on at middle elevations.

nodes.name: Fungi and bacteria
nodes.desc: Break down leaf litter, wood and dead animals, returning nutrients to the soil.

nodes.name: Hispaniolan pine
nodes.desc: The dominant pine of the open upper forest, whose seedlings do well after fire.

nodes.name: Weinmannia
nodes.desc: A cloud-forest tree genus, with Weinmannia pinnata among the broadleaf trees reported in the park.

nodes.name: Miconia shrubs
nodes.desc: Many Miconia species grow in the understory here; the genus is known for small berries that birds eat.

nodes.name: Wild ackee
nodes.desc: A fruiting forest tree whose fruits are taken by thrushes, pigeons and bananaquits.

nodes.name: Parrot weed
nodes.desc: A fast-growing shrub of forest openings whose seeds are eaten by small birds.

nodes.name: Bananaquit
nodes.desc: A small nectar-, fruit- and insect-eating bird, recorded eating Bocconia and Cupania.

nodes.name: Red-legged thrush
nodes.desc: Forages for fruit and invertebrates in the forest; recorded eating Cupania fruit.

nodes.name: Hispaniolan hutia
nodes.desc: A rare, mostly vegetarian rodent of Hispaniolan forests, found in the south-western massifs.

nodes.name: Black rat
nodes.desc: An introduced omnivorous rodent that eats seeds and fruit and is itself prey for cats, hawks and owls.

nodes.name: Trap-jaw ant
nodes.desc: A leaf-litter ant that feeds on sugary fruit and nectar and on small invertebrates.

nodes.name: Eleutherodactylus frogs
nodes.desc: Small direct-developing frogs of the forest floor; several local species are critically endangered.

nodes.name: Hispaniolan green anole
nodes.desc: A tree-dwelling lizard that hunts insects such as ants on trunks and foliage.

nodes.name: Hispaniolan lizard-cuckoo
nodes.desc: A large forest cuckoo that hunts lizards and other small animals in the canopy.

nodes.name: Hispaniolan solenodon
nodes.desc: A nocturnal insectivore that roots in soil and logs for arthropods, worms, snails and small reptiles.

nodes.name: Turkey vulture
nodes.desc: A soaring scavenger that cleans up carrion and so returns it to the food chain.

nodes.name: Red-tailed hawk
nodes.desc: A raptor that hunts rodents, lizards and birds across open slopes and forest edges.

nodes.name: Ashy-faced owl
nodes.desc: A night hunter that preys on solenodons, which evolved with few land predators.

nodes.name: Feral cat
nodes.desc: An introduced predator that kills rats, lizards and solenodons.
